daily_reality.summary: Respiratory therapists manage patients' breathing through ventilator management, oxygen therapy, airway management, and pulmonary diagnostics. They work in hospitals (ICU, ER, NICU), outpatient clinics, and home care settings providing critical respiratory care.
typical_tasks: Set up and manage mechanical ventilators for patients who cannot breathe independently
Perform arterial blood gas (ABG) sampling and analysis
Perform chest physiotherapy and airway clearance techniques
Respond to emergency codes for airway management and intubation assistance
Monitor and adjust ventilator settings based on patient response
Conduct pulmonary function tests (PFTs) for diagnostic evaluation
Educate patients on inhaler use, breathing exercises, and home equipment
Set up and maintain oxygen delivery systems
Manage BiPAP/CPAP for sleep apnea and acute respiratory failure
Document respiratory assessments and treatment in EHR

deadlines.equipment_checks: Per shift for life support equipment

daily_reality.seasonality: Respiratory caseload spikes during flu season (November-March), RSV season (fall-winter), wildfire season (summer-fall), and COVID surges. NICU workload relatively steady year-round.

regulatory.summary: NBRC (National Board for Respiratory Care) provides CRT and RRT credentials. State licensure required in all 50 states. AARC (American Association for Respiratory Care) is the primary professional body. Scope expanding in many states.

key_laws.name: State Respiratory Care Practice Acts
key_laws.detail: All 50 states, DC, and Puerto Rico require respiratory therapists to be licensed

key_laws.name: CMS Conditions of Participation
key_laws.detail: Hospitals must provide respiratory care services meeting quality standards

key_laws.name: Joint Commission Standards
key_laws.detail: Quality and safety standards for respiratory care departments

requirements: Graduate from CoARC-accredited respiratory therapy program
CRT credential (entry) — pass NBRC Therapist Multiple-Choice exam
RRT credential (advanced) — pass additional Clinical Simulation Examination
State licensure required in all states (most accept NBRC credentials)
Specialty certifications: ACCS (Adult Critical Care), NPS (Neonatal/Pediatric), SDS (Sleep Disorders)
certifying_bodies: NBRC — National Board for Respiratory Care
CoARC — Commission on Accreditation for Respiratory Care (program accreditation)

regulatory.penalties: State board can suspend/revoke license for negligence or scope violations. CMS deficiency citations for respiratory care failures. Malpractice liability for ventilator mismanagement.

tools.summary: Respiratory therapists manage mechanical ventilators (Medtronic, Hamilton, Draeger), oxygen delivery systems, ABG analyzers, and pulmonary function testing equipment. EHR documentation critical.

ABG analyzers (Radiometer ABL, Siemens RAPIDPoint)

primary_software.name: Oxygen delivery equipment (high-flow nasal cannula, Vapotherm)
EHR (Epic, Cerner) with respiratory therapy modules
primary_software.purpose: Documentation of assessments, ventilator settings, and treatments

primary_software.name: Bronchoscopy equipment
primary_software.purpose: Assisting physicians with airway visualization procedures

primary_software.name: Metabolic carts (Vyaire VMAX)
primary_software.purpose: Indirect calorimetry for nutrition assessment in ventilated patients

EHR documentation burden during high-acuity care
Integration gaps between monitoring devices and EHR

terminology.summary: Respiratory therapists use extensive pulmonary physiology, ventilator management, and critical care terminology including gas exchange parameters, ventilator modes, and respiratory pharmacology.

key_terms.meaning: Arterial Blood Gas — measures pH, PaO2, PaCO2, HCO3, SaO2
Fraction of Inspired Oxygen — concentration of oxygen delivered
Positive End-Expiratory Pressure — prevents alveolar collapse
Volume of air delivered per breath on ventilator
Assist-Control / Volume Control / Pressure Control — ventilator modes
Synchronized Intermittent Mandatory Ventilation — weaning mode
Continuous/Bilevel Positive Airway Pressure — non-invasive ventilation
Peripheral oxygen saturation — pulse oximetry reading
End-tidal CO2 — capnography monitoring of ventilation
Pulmonary Function Test — spirometry and lung volume measurement
Forced Expiratory Volume / Forced Vital Capacity — key PFT metrics
Inhaled medication that opens airways (albuterol, ipratropium)
Gradual reduction of ventilator support toward extubation
Removal of endotracheal tube from patient's airway
High-Flow Nasal Cannula — heated humidified high-flow oxygen delivery

career_psychology.summary: Respiratory therapists are critical care professionals managing life-support equipment. 13% job growth (much faster than average) reflects strong demand. Post-COVID awareness elevated profession's visibility. Burnout from ICU intensity.

career_levels.responsibilities: General respiratory care, treatments, monitoring under supervision
Independent practice, ventilator management, critical care, PFTs
ICU/NICU specialist, complex ventilator management, protocols
Department management, budgets, staffing, quality improvement

main_fears: Ventilator mismanagement leading to patient harm
Alarm fatigue leading to missed critical events
burnout_causes: ICU intensity with critically ill and dying patients
COVID pandemic impact on workforce (PTSD, exhaustion)
Emotional toll of neonatal/pediatric critical care
growth_motivation: Specialty credentials (ACCS, NPS, SDS) for higher pay and expertise
Advanced practice RT roles (emerging in some states)
Transition to PA or nursing with bridge programs
